page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, featuring 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 236 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.06 GB/sec. However, cryptographic and extended instruction performance is limited, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 10%. General integer, database, and web serving operations perform in the average range, with static web serving throughput reaching 8.04 GB/sec and Redis SET operations executing at 8.44 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is measured at 90.93 GB/sec for large-block reads and 39.96 GB/sec for writes.

Given its ARM architecture and low memory-to-CPU ratio, the D4plds_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have modest memory requirements. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage adds value for temporary data handling. This server type is suited for lightweight web serving, software compilation, basic database operations, and single-threaded compression tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications, heavy cryptography, or complex ray tracing.
description: The Microsoft Azure D4plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the Dpldsv6 family, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs on a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features a low-memory profile of 8.0 GB RAM (2.0 GB per core) and includes 236 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong single-threaded gzip compression performance alongside average capabilities in web serving, software compilation, and database operations. However, it exhibits weaker performance in cryptographic tasks and memory-intensive benchmarks. The D4plds_v6 represents a cost-efficient option for compute-focused workloads with small memory footprints, such as lightweight web servers, application build pipelines, and basic data processing tasks.
